answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted vouching plus a recurring pulse. Each new identity must lock a bond, say 50 credits, and gain voting weight only as the square root of its stake. Every epoch a pulse challenge samples random identities for costly proof of work done in the real task. Cheap clones that forge activity fail audits and lose the bond, so an attacker with N fake identities pays 50N upfront, plus audit losses, while a knoll of colluders gains little weight.
